 Warriors Rekindle Rivalry WIth Road Contest At UTEP
 Story Links
 HONOLULU – After a 22-year hiatus, the University of Hawai'i football team and UTEP will meet once against as conference rivals when the teams face off in a Mountain West contest on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff is 7:30 p.m. MT (4:30 p.m. HT) at the Sun Bowl. Hawai'i and UTEP last met on the gridiron in 2004 when both were members of the Western Athletic Conference. The teams are now part of a new-look Mountain West with UH coming off a  56-21 win at conference newcomer Northern Illinois on Oct. 24. The Miners fell at North Dakota State, 31-7, on Oct. 31 in a meeting between first-year Mountain West programs.  
 HAWAI'I (2-6, 1-4 MW) vs. UTEP (1-7, 0-4 MW) 
 Date | Time 
 Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026 | 7:30 p.m. MT / 4:30 p.m. HT 
 Location | Stadium 
 El Paso, Texas | Sun Bowl (45,971)

 SERIES VS UTEP 
 Series Information : UH leads, 18-13
            In Honolulu: UH leads, 12-5
            In El Paso: UTEP leads, 8-6
 GAME STORYLINES 
 Hawai'i and UTEP will meet for the first time since 2004 and the 32nd time overall, with UH owning an 18-13 all-time record against the Miners.
 The two teams were members of the Western Athletic Conference together from 1979-2004, with UH holding a 15-9 advantage when the two teams meet as conference foes.
 The Warriors are 6-8 all-time against UTEP in El Paso, dropping three of the last four meetings there. UH's last win in El Paso came in 2002 (31-6).
 UH's last win over the Miners came in 2003 in Honolulu, when HC Timmy Chang threw for 426 yards and three TDs to lead the Warriors to a 31-15 win.
 The Warriors will be playing their first game since the passing of legendary head coach June Jones. Jones is the program's all-time winningest coach and coached five members of the UH coaching staff, including Chang who became the NCAA's all-time leading passer under Jones' guidance.
 In nine years under Jones, UH finished in the top four nationally in passing each season running the Run N' Shoot offense that produced numerous record-setting QBs such Chang and Heisman Trophy finalist Colt Brennan.
 UH is looking to build off of a 56-21 win at Northern Illinois the last time out. The win gave the Warriors their first Mountain West win of the year and snapped a four-game losing streak.
 The Warriors matched a program single-game scoring record for a Mountain West game against the Huskies with 56 points while forcing five turnovers in a game for the first time since 2021.
 QB Micah Alejado is third nationally with 25.7 completions per game and 202 total pass completions. He also leads the Mountain West in passing yards per game (273.3) and total offense (276.3).
 Alejado earned Mountain West Offensive Player of the Week honors after his last outing at Northern Illinois on Oct. 24, when he threw for 323 yards and three touchdowns, completing 22-of-32 passes.
 UH is looking to win the second half of a back-to-back road game stretch for the first time since 2014 at San Jose State (13-0). The Warriors have lost the second game of a back-to-back road contests six straight times.
